items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: we have Frank Foster... he’s going to play with us. It’s so wonderful to have Frank Foster

ctx.x: And tell me about the group you have right now, the Golden Men of Jazz.
Oh, the Golden Men of Jazz, we’re at the Blue Note next week, and we have such outstanding players, well we have Frank Foster, who has just left from directing the Basie © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

items.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998
items.q: And there was another place called the Topper Ballroom, it was the first place I saw Lionel Hampton’s band

ctx.x: What was the musical atmosphere that was going on that made gigs so available?

Well that was during the dance band era. There were lots of dances, mostly dances and some night club gigs like for small combos. But lots of dances by the big bands. Those were all the gigs. Concerts hadn’t started to be a thing as yet. So I played with two local big bands, three local big bands, before I formed my own band, and I played for senior proms and things like that, and other little public dances. And the scene in Cincinnati, the © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

musical scene overall was very good at the time. There were some great musicians that were from Cincinnati and there was a place called the Cotton Club which was the main nightclub venue where they had shows, productions. Then there was a dance hall called the Coliseum where all the prominent big bands came through every Sunday, so each Sunday there was a different big band, from Erskine Hawkins to Duke Ellington, Stan Kenton, to Tony Pastor, Count Basie, and that’s where I saw a good many of the big bands. And…

items.q: At that time she was Betty Bebop with Lionel Hampton, I think.

ctx.x: Anna May [Lillie Mae Jones], whatever her last name was.

At that time she was Betty Bebop with Lionel Hampton, I think. But all these musicians. I thought wow, man, there’s so many musicians in Detroit, so much happening, so many clubs on the west side, on the east end, and on the north side.
